mainEntity.name: Is it painful to switch from bonding to veneers?

acceptedAnswer.text: The process of having veneers placed typically involves a small amount of enamel removal, which is carried out under local anaesthetic to ensure your comfort. Most patients report that the procedure is straightforward and not significantly uncomfortable. Some temporary sensitivity may occur after the enamel preparation, but this usually settles within a few days. Your dentist would discuss the process in detail beforehand so you know exactly what to expect at each stage of treatment.

mainEntity.name: How long do porcelain veneers last compared to bonding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Porcelain veneers are generally expected to last between ten and fifteen years, and sometimes longer, with appropriate care. Composite bonding typically lasts between three and seven years before it may need repair or replacement. However, these are general estimates — actual longevity depends on individual factors such as oral hygiene habits, dietary choices, whether you grind your teeth, and the specific teeth involved. Your dentist can give you a more personalised indication based on your clinical assessment.

mainEntity.name: Can veneers be placed over existing bonding?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, existing composite bonding would need to be removed before veneers are placed. This is because veneers require a clean, properly prepared enamel surface to achieve a strong and reliable bond. Placing a veneer over old composite material could compromise the fit and longevity of the restoration. During your consultation, your dentist would carefully remove any existing bonding and assess the underlying tooth structure before proceeding with veneer preparation.

Not all patients are suitable candidates for porcelain veneers. Factors such as insufficient enamel, active gum disease, significant tooth grinding, or certain bite issues may mean that alternative treatments would be more appropriate. Some patients may benefit from orthodontic treatment, composite bonding, or dental crowns instead. A thorough clinical examination is essential to determine the most suitable approach for your individual dental situation and cosmetic goals.

Modern porcelain veneers are designed to closely replicate the appearance of natural teeth. The porcelain material reflects light similarly to natural enamel, and veneers are custom-made to match the colour, shape, and proportions of your existing teeth. Your dentist and the dental laboratory work together to ensure a natural-looking result. During the planning stage, you would typically have the opportunity to discuss shade preferences and see previews of the expected outcome before committing to the final result.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my bonding needs replacing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs that bonding may need attention include visible staining that doesn't respond to cleaning, chips or rough edges, a noticeable difference in colour compared to your natural teeth, or a feeling that the bonding surface has become uneven. Your dentist can assess the condition of existing bonding during a routine check-up and advise you on whether repair, replacement, or an alternative approach may be appropriate. Regular dental visits help ensure any issues are identified early.
